dedupe_keys.name: comparing the accuracy of energy prediction models based on hourly and daily mean outdoor temperature

description: Kuru, Merve and colleagues publish this resource through Zenodo. This completed application models HVAC electricity using outdoor temperature in a commercial building in Saint-Quentin-en-Yvelines. Measurements cover January to December 2015. Daily mean temperature and daily consumption have a reported correlation of 0.82, compared with 0.70 for the hourly representation. The result concerns this aggregation comparison and does not establish that daily data always outperform hourly forecasting. The paper supports checking the temporal inputs used in building-energy prediction. It does not itself establish that the underlying observations are independently downloadable or identical to the Challenger collection. Native metadata gives open access and the licence label cc-by-4.0. These terms describe the deposit; a paper licence does not establish a software licence. Coverage is limited to the stated sites, model settings and application examples. Only descriptive metadata and file descriptors were inspected. Linked data, code and document bodies were not opened.
